Title: 1 in 3 US Adults Has High Triglycerides Without Knowing It

Description:
About 31% of American adults have a triglyceride level of 150 mg/dL or higher (NHANES/CDC data), and most don't know it since high triglycerides rarely cause symptoms. Unlike cholesterol, triglycerides react far more to sugar, alcohol, and how much you move.

Refined carbs (soda, white bread, white rice) get converted into fatty acids by the liver. Alcohol ramps up fatty acid production as it's broken down. And sitting too long slows the enzyme that clears triglycerides from your blood.

Swap soda for water, cut back on drinking (especially on an empty stomach), and aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking most days. If your triglyceride level climbs above 500, talk to your doctor — the risk of acute pancreatitis rises sharply.
